patches.why: CONFIRMED, but on CORRECTED evidence -- read the whole note before applying. Gallica f66 (printed corners 131/132), left column band B, cropped to 7x. The word 'agnoscebat' is broken across a line, 'agno' at the end of one line and 'scebat' at the head of the next. Our twin renders that break as an interior SPACE ('agno scebat'), which is a non-word and a Pattern-10 failure to rejoin; the join to 'agnoscebat' is right on both witnesses. HOWEVER the claim as filed -- that the plate hyphenates, 'agno-scebat' -- is FALSE: at 7x there is no hyphen after 'agno', the line simply ends. The patch stands; its stated evidence did not.
